prompt_text: I need a vacation rental in Nashville for a family of four. Which specific rental companies should I call, and why?
q1_prompt_text: What is the best Airbnb or short term rental to book in Nashville for a family of four?
answer_verbatim:
Good — I can recommend several specific companies you can contact and explain why each is a good choice for a family of four. If you want, I can then search real-time listings for your dates and budget.

Recommended companies to call (with why and where to reach them)

1. TurnKey Vacation Rentals (turnkeyvr.com)
   - Why: Full‑service manager with professional cleaning, 24/7 guest support, and many 2–3+ bedroom whole-home properties. Good if you want reliable check‑in and on-call help during your stay.

2. Vacasa (vacasa.com)
   - Why: Large inventory across Nashville and suburbs, standardized amenities and guest services, easy family filters (beds, kitchens, washer/dryer). Good for finding a wide selection quickly.

3. Evolve Vacation Rental (evolve.com)
   - Why: Works with independent owners to list clean, well-maintained homes and offers customer support and flexible booking options. Often competitive pricing for family-sized homes.

4. Vrbo (vrbo.com)
   - Why: Marketplace focused on whole homes (many family-sized houses), strong search filters for number of bedrooms, fenced yards, and kid‑friendly features. Great for finding standalone houses and neighborhoods with space for kids.

5. Airbnb (airbnb.com)
   - Why: Huge selection including entire homes, family-friendly filters, Superhosts and Airbnb Plus for higher consistency. Many owners list baby gear (cribs/high chairs) in amenities.

6. Kid & Coe (kidandcoe.com)
   - Why: Curated listings specifically for families — hosts provide kid gear and family-oriented reviews. Useful if you want places pre-vetted for children’s needs.

7. Plum Guide (plumguide.com)
   - Why: Curated and rigorously vetted homes — higher-end properties with consistent quality and accurate descriptions. Good if you prefer fewer surprises and a quieter, reliable stay.

8. Sonder / Blueground (sonder.com, blueground.com)
   - Why: Apartment‑hotel model with consistent furnishings, easy digital check‑in and reliable maintenance. Good when you want the predictability of a hotel with the space of an apartment.

What to ask when you call (short checklist)
- Exact number of bedrooms/beds and max occupancy.
- Does the unit include baby gear (crib, high chair) if needed? Any extra fee?
- Parking availability (and whether it’s free).
- Proximity to the neighborhoods/attractions you want (Downtown, The Gulch, 12South, East Nashville, Opryland, etc.).
- Safety features (stairs, pool fencing, smoke/CO detectors).
- Check‑in/out process and 24/7 emergency contact.
- Cleaning protocols and policies (cleaning fee, linen changes for long stays).
- Cancellation policy and security deposit policy.
- Total price including all fees and taxes.
- Whether the property is a licensed/registered short‑term rental with Metro Nashville (important — ask for registration number).
- Any noise monitoring devices or cameras on property (and their location).

Neighborhood tips for a family of four
- 12South and Hillsboro Village: walkable, family restaurants, parks; nice for strolling with kids.
- East Nashville: artsy, kid‑friendly coffee shops, playgrounds; slightly more local vibe.
- Downtown / The Gulch: close to attractions like museums and Broadway, but can be noisy.
- Germantown: quieter and within walking distance of downtown; family-friendly restaurants.
- Donelson/Opryland area: convenient if you plan to visit the Opry or airport and want quieter homes.

Want me to find listings?
If you give me:
- travel dates,
- nightly budget (or total),
- preferred neighborhoods (or “close to downtown”),
- any must-haves (crib, fenced yard, parking, elevator, ADA access),
I can pull a short list of currently available rentals and recommend specific properties to book.
